jokes.punchline: 'Again?' implies this has happened before — Corporate America has previously destroyed Britta's love life. Then she calls out 'Subway!' to a stranger, suggesting she doesn't remember what her love interest actually looks like either.
jokes.explanation: 'Again?' is a good one-word callback implying Britta has a pattern. The stranger-as-Subway moment is a nice visual confusion beat. Good economy. 'Corporate America has destroyed love' is a Britta line of the first order — political grievance as emotional response.

jokes.text: New Subway appears: 'Britta, you silly. It is me, Subway.' — it's a different person. 'What? I had a great time with you last night in the pillow fort, the one exception being the deviant sex act you initiated without my consent. Eat fresh.'
jokes.setup: Britta has just called out 'Subway!' to a stranger
jokes.punchline: The stranger IS Subway — but a different Subway. The corporation has simply replaced one corpohumanoid with another. This one has the same memories (or briefing) but delivers the horrifying note that there was a 'deviant sex act you initiated without my consent' — implying Pierce's recording was used as an orientation briefing.
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's funniest and most structurally brilliant moments. The reveal that Subway is replaceable — a corporate product, not a person — is both the satirical thesis and an earned, devastating punchline. 'The deviant sex act you initiated without my consent' delivered as a casual briefing note, combined with 'Eat fresh' as a conversation-closer, is perfect. This joke had to be built over the entire episode to land this way. The final 'Eat fresh' takes on a completely different tone — creepy, clinical, final. High marks across the board.

jokes.text: Britta screams after New Subway's 'Eat fresh.' Everyone reacts. Dean Pelton arrives: 'There is a situation developing in the study room. I would elaborate, but I am out of breath because I walked here very briskly.'
jokes.setup: The Dean arrives dramatically with urgent news about the fort conflict
jokes.punchline: 'I would elaborate, but I am out of breath because I walked here very briskly' — the Dean undercuts his own dramatic entrance by citing light exercise as the reason he can't continue
jokes.explanation: Classic Dean Pelton moment. The elaborate non-explanation ('I would elaborate, but...') followed by the bathetic reason ('walked here very briskly') is perfectly in character. The Dean always has the wrong gear for every situation. High economy.

jokes.text: In the study room standoff, Dean Pelton: 'Can we just flip a coin to decide who has to back down?' Both: 'No.' 'Well, I'm Dean, so I'm making the call. The pillow fort comes down.'
jokes.setup: The Dean is trying to arbitrate the fort conflict peacefully
jokes.punchline: His coin flip compromise is immediately rejected by both sides, so he invokes his authority — and immediately uses it against Abed. 'Well, I'm Dean' as a legal argument is funny coming from an authority figure who is never taken seriously.
jokes.explanation: Functional institutional comedy. The Dean's faux authority landing on Abed is predictable but serves the plot. Not particularly inventive.

jokes.text: During the fort standoff: 'Watch it, Star-Burns.' Star-Burns: 'My name is Alex!'
jokes.setup: Physical confrontation is breaking out between fort partisans
jokes.punchline: Star-Burns insisting on 'Alex' is a recurring bit in the season — he's trying to rebrand but nobody respects the new name
jokes.explanation: Running gag that lands on recognition for regular viewers. 'My name is Alex!' with Star-Burns' full indignation is a reliable bit. Not high-craft but it's efficient and characteristically Community — background character detail elevated.

jokes.text: The fort conflict erupts into full war: 'This is war!' — declared with complete seriousness about a blanket fort vs. pillow fort dispute
jokes.setup: The Dean's ruling has not resolved the conflict; both forts have dug in
jokes.punchline: The declaration of war over a pillow fort vs. blanket fort dispute, treated with the full gravity of an actual military conflict, is the comedic escalation the episode has been building toward
jokes.explanation: The 'war' declaration works because the entire episode has been building the stakes of the blanket/pillow fort distinction with complete sincerity. The payoff — full warfare over craft standards — is earned by the thematic work of the episode. It's also the classic Community escalation move: start with a mundane disagreement, end with a declaration of war. Good structural payoff.

jokes.text: Tag scene: Vice Dean Laybourne is briefed. 'Sir, it appears that Troy Barnes' blanket fort may go to war with Abed Nadir's pillow fort.' Laybourne: 'Of course. Soon Troy and Abed will be torn asunder, and an unencumbered Troy will turn to his destiny... The air conditioning repair school.'
jokes.setup: The final scene reveals that the entire fort conflict may be a manipulation by Laybourne
jokes.punchline: The air conditioning repair school as the ultimate prize in an elaborate Machiavellian scheme — for which Laybourne is willing to destroy a friendship — is an absurd anticlimax perfectly proportioned to the show
jokes.explanation: Strong ending beat. Laybourne's cold-blooded manipulation of an entire friendship to recruit one student to an air conditioning repair school is the ultimate Community joke about institutional absurdity. 'How unfortunate for Troy and Abed' delivered by someone who manufactured the misfortune is both funny and genuinely dark. Good rewatch bonus — Laybourne's earlier scenes read completely differently knowing he's orchestrating the whole thing.

jokes.text: Final shot: Laybourne aide says 'You are a cold-blooded man, sir.' Laybourne: 'Yes.' Then: 'See you in band practice.'
jokes.setup: Laybourne has just been called cold-blooded for orchestrating the Troy/Abed fracture
jokes.punchline: 'See you in band practice' — the menacing closer is immediately deflated by the mundane social obligation, suggesting these two sinister schemers also play in a band together
jokes.explanation: Perfect button for the episode. The bathos of 'See you in band practice' deflates the whole sinister tableau. The aide confirmed in a band with his manipulative Vice Dean boss is an unexpected detail that humanizes/absurdizes the whole conspiracy. Very economical four-word punchline.

tmdb_overview: When Britta falls for the human embodiment of the Subway sandwich chain, Shirley and Pierce hope to use the situation to their advantage.
insight: Virtual paintball tournament premise sustains 59 jokes across soft-landing absurdist escalations.
